messages:
Lina (CSE): FYI Fluxly just reported a surge of 429s during their onboarding run. They say it happens when server workers bump ephemeral creds simultaneously after a deploy.

Lina (CSE): Quote from Fluxly: \"we run a few hundred background workers that call embed() on job start; after nightly rotate, ~30% of jobs got 429 and retried, causing a second wave.\"

fluxly-sre: Here are their logs: `2026-04-05T08:12:03Z POST /v1/embeddings 429 rate_limit tenant=fluxly job_id=job-7345` then `2026-04-05T08:12:04Z ephemeral refresh ok id=tkn_zz12` then retries. They saw ~120 concurrent inits for ~15s.

Harish (Platform): Sounds like a thundering herd on ephemeral refresh + preflight. Are they using server sdk v2.x with warmup disabled? Any prefetch concurrency config?

Lina (CSE): They're on node-sdk 2.0.1, warmup=false, and each worker fetches ephemeral token on start. No client-side splay.

Priya (SDK): Recommending quick fixes: 1) add a shared token cache per process (fetch once, reuse for job batch); 2) add randomized jitter for initial preflight (50-300ms); 3) exponential backoff on 429 with small cap for init calls. We can ship a patch to 2.0.x today.

Harish (Platform): Ops-side mitigation: we can temporarily allow a small burst window for onboarding tenants and add a short-lived high-concurrency slot for their tenant. Also consider increasing ephemeral grace from 2s -> 8s in cluster to reduce overlap. @deploy-bot were there token service changes today?

deploy-bot: Deploy note: token-service change rolled at 2026-04-05T03:00:15Z: tightened rotate interval for opaque tokens (owner: infra/security). No grace change.

Lina (CSE): Fluxly asked if we can apply tenant-level QPS smoothing while they patch. They need a quick workaround or they'll delay rollout (possible renewal risk if onboarding stalls).

ops-oncall: I can add a tenant smoothing rule for tenant=fluxly for next 2 hours and monitor. Applying now.

fluxly-sre: After smoothing applied at 08:20 UTC, errors dropped from 30% -> 2% for new job starts. Good signal.

Priya (SDK): I'll open PR #SDK-719: \"node-sdk: process-level token cache + init jitter\" and cut a patch release 2.0.2. Patch includes sample code: ```js
// simple per-process token cache
let _cachedToken = null;
async function getToken(){
  if(_cachedToken && Date.now() < _cachedToken.expiresAt) return _cachedToken.value;
  const t = await fetch('/.auth/ephemeral');
  _cachedToken = { value: t.token, expiresAt: Date.now() + 45_000 };
  return t.token;
}
```

Harish (Platform): Follow-ups: 1) revert the tightened rotate interval in canary until SDK patch is validated; 2) add onboarding playbook entry about server-worker token caching; 3) add a CloudWatch/Grafana dashboard panel for concurrent init spikes per tenant so CSE can watch.

Lina (CSE): I'll schedule a 30-min runbook session with Fluxly to walk through the SDK patch and help them deploy. Also flagging renewal touchpoint: if they hit another onboarding blocker we'll escalate to AM.

ops-oncall: Tenant smoothing removed at 09:50 UTC after validation. No regressions observed.

Priya (SDK): 2.0.2 released at 09:10 UTC with the token cache + jitter and backoff. Added docs in SDK README about recommended defaults and server worker patterns.

fluxly-sre: Confirmed rolling deploy using 2.0.2 reduced init errors to near zero. Thanks for quick turnaround.

Lina (CSE): Closing the loop with the customer and adding KB draft to internal wiki (will share link). Marking account health as green and scheduling renewal check-in next week. :thumbsup:

Harish (Platform): Created infra ticket INF-2154 to track rotate-interval revert and monitoring tasks.

Lina (CSE): Great work team — good example of CSE+SDK+Ops coordination on onboarding.\"
